issues.description: The full supplied Tables 3 and 4 workflow consumes confidential GSS2010 and GSSpanel data. The package inventory lists only GSSstate.dta, which the README describes as a state list, so the necessary prepared GSS analysis inputs are absent from this package and require an authorized compatible route or clarification.

JAR_T7&8.do line 1 contains a placeholder path through Data and code for publication, while the actual packaged bankfees.dta is at the package root. Use a relative bankfees.dta path from an isolated working copy of that root.

Table 3 Panel A reads banked2011 at JAR_T1 to T6.do line 74. The earlier Table 2 block creates a tempfile named banked, not a file or alias named banked2011; no supplied producer or package file closes this handoff.

All supplied programs use bare basenames without a cd command. input data.do writes with save ..., replace into the launch-time current directory, including names that are also packaged inputs. Run only in an isolated writable working copy and configure a coherent current directory per branch; do not overwrite the frozen package data.

The supplied Table 6 city preparation merges bank_data_city at input data.do line 247, but no producer for that intermediate appears in the supplied preparation program and no bank_data_city file appears in the frozen package inventory. It is not the same as the packaged final bank_city.dta.

input data.do repeatedly uses banked_metro as a raw metro_number/year/banked source, then saves the normalized state/placea/year/avg_banked result back under banked_metro. In a shared current directory this replaces the raw source before later blocks reopen it. The packaged same-name file matches only the normalized output schema; preserve separate raw and prepared locations and obtain the intended reset/branch contract.

input data.do creates complaints.dta from Consumer_complaints_all but its keep list omits WF. The Table 4 state branch in JAR_T1 to T6.do reads WF from complaints.dta, while the packaged direct-analysis complaints table contains WF. Keep the prepared package table separate and clarify how the prep branch is meant to supply WF before treating its output as the Table 4 input.

The packaged census_st.dta exposes percapinc, which matches Table 4, but Table 3 Panel B reads percapitainc after merging that table. No rename or derived variable bridges the names. Confirm the intended source-column mapping before editing or running that branch.

The supplied merge statements retain legacy key syntax and branch-specific _merge/drop/PR overrides, but one-row metadata cannot establish key uniqueness or full periods. Preserve each authored key, filter and sample rule; do not infer 1:1 cardinality or extend date ranges. Validate key counts and required date coverage only when the complete input data are available.

Confirm whether the state and two city trust inputs are separate author-prepared products; do not treat one same-purpose-looking basename as a substitute for another.
validation: After authorized availability is confirmed, compare bounded metadata for each file with the distinct state or city merge keys and trust fields used by input data.do.

Provide the exact authorized Complaints_city_trust2010.dta input or its supplied producer, and document how its complaint and trust columns were formed; do not infer that input from complaints_city.dta or citytrust10.dta.

actions.description: When the complete compatible inputs are available, validate merge keys and required history while preserving each authored merge statement, _merge handling, PR override, sample filter, one-year complaint lead, and forward-fill operation.
steps: Before execution, inspect duplicate counts on the actual authored merge keys and confirm the record units and date/year fields of each participating input.
Check the coverage needed by each supplied branch, including the complaint-year shift and the years added/filled around tsfill; do not infer a 1:1 merge or extend the authors' analysis sample.
Record the results and retain the original merge cardinality syntax and all authored filters and branch-specific sample rules.

actions.description: Set up isolated writable working copies and a documented branch-specific current-directory plan for the bare-basename Stata programs; retain raw and prepared files separately and do not launch the monolithic preparation chain until its repeated-input reset contract is resolved.
steps: Copy the supplied sources and any authorized inputs into isolated working directories; preserve the frozen package files and keep the original package read-only.
Because the scripts use bare basenames, document the current directory for each preparation branch and analysis entry point, including where each output will be written.

Keep raw banked_metro in a separate location from the normalized city-year banked_metro output and do not execute the full preparation chain in one shared directory until the source-supported reset or branch-specific input contract is known.

After all required source and handoff contracts are resolved, produce and validate the intended preparation outputs before running JAR_T1 to T6.do with its compatible inputs; run JAR_T7&8.do independently from the package-root working copy described in A001.
Preserve Stata's observed varabbrev on setting so the post-rename company prefix can resolve to companycpb; do not add a second company field or change the authored grouping.
validation: Before any authorized run, verify that every bare input resolves in the documented branch directory, every write lands in that branch's working copy, and the package's frozen inputs remain unchanged.
Keep the full workflow unresolved until the repeated raw/prepared banked_metro reads, required producers, and branch output paths are all accounted for.

actions.description: Make the author-required carryforward and cluster2 commands available from an approved Stata adopath before attempting Table 3 Panel B, then verify the exact command entry points.
steps: Obtain or identify only an author-compatible, institution-approved copy of carryforward and cluster2 and configure its location on the Stata adopath; no package is installed during this assessment.
Preserve the authored carry-forward call and cluster2 specification.
validation: From the intended Stata environment, run which carryforward and which cluster2 and confirm each resolves to the approved ado file before any authorized analysis run.

review_notes: No author program, study dataset, or estimator was executed. Software checks were limited to Stata version/which/query metadata; packaged-data inspections used the assigned bounded one-row probes.

The independent analysis-only scope is supported by the supplied JAR_T7&8.do and packaged bankfees.dta, whose bounded probe contains all 11 consumed fields; the README describes 2002–2006 and 2011–2015 coverage, while the one-row probe does not establish complete historical coverage. No analysis was run.

The full pipeline remains unresolved because the prepared GSS2010/GSSpanel inputs and multiple raw preparation contracts or producers are absent or unverified. No NORC contact, eligibility check, form, contract request, or data acquisition was made.

Authored merge keys, merge syntax, filters, sample overrides, the one-year complaint lead, tsfill, and banked carry-forward are retained as written. No 1:1 cardinality, broader period, or new variable definition is inferred.

Stata 18 reports varabbrev on, making company a valid unique prefix of companycpb after the supplied rename in the observed source state; no company-field repair is proposed. The earlier incomplete varabbrev query and its corrected metadata check are both preserved in probes.

The normalized packaged banked_metro.dta is a supported direct-analysis input, but it does not satisfy the raw metro_number/year/banked contract; raw and normalized locations and repeated branch resets remain unresolved.
